transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-02-22 15:00 UTC
Duration: 56 mins
Attendees:
 - Maya Li (Redwood AE)
 - Jasper Cole (Redwood SE)
 - Priya Narayanan (Redwood CSM)
 - Carlos Mendez (Peregrine Head of ML Ops)
 - Ruth Kim (Peregrine VP Eng)

 - Liam O'Neill (Peregrine Finance)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete): Quarterly health + runway planning. Usage spikes during holiday pilot. Discussed Dedicated quota, private deployment windows, and model rollforward staging.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Okay everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood — I'll kick us off, we have Jasper and Priya on the call as well. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Carlos: Good, thanks. Busy coming out of the pilot week, lots to cover.
[00:12] Ruth: Yeah, hi, quick heads up — Liam's on for cost questions.
[00:16] Liam: Hey all.
[00:18] Maya: Great. Agenda: run through usage patterns, cost drivers, recent incidents and mitigations, then roadmap and rollforward plan. If we hit the big asks early we can jump into the 8k latency bench. Sound good?
[00:29] Anika: Yep. We'll probably need the bench, our peak weekend rhythm is still our biggest concern.
[00:33] Jasper: Quick note — there might be transcription mismatch on some infra words, I might call out KV cache as K V cash in the notes.
[00:39] Carlos: (laughs) that's fine. I'll start with usage snapshot. Our product traffic, token wise, spiked by 3.8x over the holiday pilot window, median seq length moved from ~350 to 1.2k because customers used richer context for returns. Peak concurrency hit ~420 rps, which is what kicked our alerts.
[01:02] Priya: Do you have the breakdown of embeddings vs generation tokens?
[01:05] Carlos: Yeah — embeddings were about 22% of tokens but 55% of requests. The big driver is smaller batch sizes for embeddings which kills throughput.
[01:15] Ruth: We're also seeing more multimodal prep steps upstream but that's on our tech debt list.
[01:20] Jasper: On the Redwood side, batching and automatic prefix caching can recoup a lot of that cost. If you can push larger embedding batches we'll see unit cost drop 30–40% in many cases.
[01:32] Anika: Our concern is latency; we can't add latency to customer flows, even if it saves cost.
[01:38] Maya: That's the classic latency vs cost tradeoff — we can present configurations that maintain 95p latency SLO while increasing batching for background flows.
[01:46] Carlos: Can you be specific about model variants? We tried a quantized 4-bit drop in one test last month and saw some jitter.
[01:53] Jasper: Sure, the jitter usually comes from kernel selection variability on mixed batch sizes, especially when sequence lengths vary. We recommend a staged rollforward: canary on non-critical routes, then dedicated pools for consistent throughput.
[02:05] Ruth: Dedicated pools — pricing and burst policy?
[02:09] Maya: We'll sketch pricing today. Dedicated gives you reserved GPUs with predictable throughput; burst policies let you exceed commit for short windows — good for that 3.8x holiday spike. We'll send options for weekend burst caps vs flat commit.
[02:21] Liam: From finance, does Dedicated lock us into a minimum spend? We need runway scenarios.
[02:25] Maya: Yes, there are commit tiers. We can model a blended scenario: smaller baseline commit + burst credits. We'll show a 6- and 12-month case.
[02:33] Carlos: What about Private / VPC deployments? We have compliance requirements for some customer data.
[02:38] Priya: We've onboarded two customers on Private in the last quarter; it's a private control plane plus optional on-prem. For Peregrine, we usually recommend a hybrid: control plane in Redwood, inference nodes in VPC.
[02:50] Anika: How about audit logs and KMS integration? Our security team wants envelope encryption and customer-managed keys.
[02:56] Jasper: We support KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs. Priya will share the SOC2 addendum and the KMS spec after this call.
[03:03] Priya: I'll send the docs today, expect the addendum and an encryption matrix.
[03:06] Teo: On the rollforward — what's the timeline to move to newer model family? We're planning a feature that depends on the LLM upgrade in Q2.
[03:13] Jasper: Two parts: model admission and production serving. Admission (evals + prompt tuning) we can help with in 2–3 weeks. Serving: we suggest a canary + auto-fallback to older model if latency regresses. Full rollforward safe window typically 4–6 weeks with good test coverage.
[03:27] Ruth: We need an explicit rollback plan — our last rollout created a spike in token usage for a misrouted route.
[03:33] Maya: We'll include runbook snippets: canary thresholds, traffic split, and automatic fallback policy.
[03:40] Carlos: About reliability incidents — we had two short outages during peak when our autoscale triggers were delayed. Any suggestions?
[03:46] Jasper: Autoscale delay usually from burst demand that exceeds provisioning time. Recommend a warm pool and faster horizontal scale on control path. Also pre-warming for known events (marketing pushes).
[03:57] Anika: How intrusive is warm pool to costs?
[03:59] Maya: You pay for reserved capacity; we can size it to critical minimum. We did a quick calc: a small warm pool covering 20% of peak reduces outage risk by ~80% while adding ~12% to committed spend — numbers will be in the pricing sketch.
[04:18] Liam: We'll need that in an ROI format — added cost vs outage cost avoided, with assumptions.
[04:23] Maya: We'll add a one-pager ROI with assumptions.
[04:26] Teo: Any concerns about model quality regressions with quantization? Our product depends on precision for returns summarization.
[04:33] Jasper: For summarization, 4-bit quantization can be workable but needs targeted evals. We'll run regen tests on your prompt set. Also consider intermediate 8-bit quant profiles.
[04:44] Carlos: Can Redwood run the bench with our 10k prompt sample?
[04:48] Jasper: Yes, if you can share anonymized prompts and token counts. We'll run 8k sequence latency bench and a quantization QA pass.
[04:56] Carlos: We can share a scrubbed CSV — action item.
[04:58] (brief static noise)
[05:00] [05:00] Priya: Quick note — sometimes the transcripts say 'K V cash' instead of KV cache — ignore that in the doc.
[05:06] (laughter)
[05:08] Ruth: Security — what about SSO / SAML and RBAC?
[05:12] Jasper: Full SSO/SAML supported, SCIM provisioning, RBAC with route-level controls. We'll include role maps.
[05:19] Teo: Are there any competitors we should watch for in terms of price or feature?
[05:22] Maya: We discussed Anthropic and OpenAI, and AWS Bedrock was mentioned for marketplace bundling, particularly for multi-cloud procurement heuristics.
[05:33] Anika: For the bench run, can we get a runbook template so our SREs can reproduce locally?
[05:38] Jasper: Yes — I'll attach a step-by-step: dataset scrape, anonymization, run harness invocation, and result interpretation.
[05:45] Carlos: On observability, we need token-level cost breakdown by route and model variant. Your Console showed good detail but we want per-customer routing.
[05:55] Priya: Token-level by route is available; per-customer routing will need the route tags from your side. If you tag customer ids upstream we can correlate in the Console.
[06:06] Ruth: We'll add tagging in the next sprint.
[06:09] Liam: One procurement thing — do you support Net 60?
[06:12] Maya: Standard is Net 30 for hosted, but for enterprise Dedicated we can negotiate Net 60 on contract. We'll flag finance for that.
[06:20] (brief pause)
[06:22] Carlos: I'd like to recap what we need from Redwood and what we'll provide.
[06:26] Maya: Sure — Redwood deliverables: pricing sketch for Dedicated + burst, SOC2 addendum and KMS spec, 8k latency bench results, runbook snippets for canary/rollback, ROI one-pager.
[06:39] Carlos: Peregrine deliverables: anonymized traffic CSV, peak weekend forecast, tag rollout plan for per-customer routing, decision on baseline commit by 3/10.
[06:51] Teo: On the rollforward, if we can get the canary in March we'll align with product launch in April.
[06:57] Jasper: That timeline seems doable provided the bench shows acceptable latency and quality.
[07:02] Ruth: Any blockers on security?
[07:05] Priya: Not on Redwood's side; we'll provide the addendum and options for KMS.
[07:09] Carlos: A practical question — for weekend bursts, do we get auto-fallback to hosted model variants if Dedicated is saturated?
[07:16] Maya: Yes — smart routing can fail over to compatible hosted variants by policy; we'll include cost and latency deltas in the sketch.
[07:25] Liam: Can that routing be audited? For bill reconciliation.
[07:29] Jasper: Yes, all routing decisions are traceable in the Console logs and we can export a csv for finance reconciliation.
[07:36] Carlos: Great. Anything else?
[07:38] Teo: One last thing — will Redwood help with prompt sets for the rollforward eval?
[07:42] Jasper: We can help curate and run the evals with your product prompts.
[07:46] Maya: Ok, we've got clear actions. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the items within the dates discussed.
[07:52] Ruth: Thanks all.
[07:54] Liam: Thanks.
[07:55] Carlos: Thanks.
[07:56] (meeting ends)
